The generation voltage for power generating units is considered 13.8 kV for the GT generator and 13.2 kV for the BPT generator. The generators are connected to the 138 kV system at the main GIS over 13.8/138 kV and 13.2/138 kV generator transformers of adequate ratings, respectively. 480V is selected for low voltage distribution as well as utilization voltage within various plant units. Description 1 35301-97A-000-ELE-0001-RA Single-line diagram of the overall system 2 35301-97A-000-ELE-0002-R0 Sub-station layout 7.0 Water System 7.1 Recirculating Water System A closed loop indirect circulating water system is considered for equipment cooling in the secondary circuit of heat exchangers of CCS to bring down the temperature to 90oF. It is also used for cooling of rotating equipment bearings, jackets, lube, seal oil, and intercoolers. The new cooling tower is located near the CCU. The main component of the indirect cooling water (ICW) system is a mechanical induced-draft cooling tower counter flow type with FRP construction and with PVC fills with basin, ICW circulation pumps, chemical injection facilities, and ICW Distribution and Collection Headers. Circulation water is cooled in the 5-cell cooling tower from a bulk return temperature of 120°F down to 90°F based on 75°F wet bulb temperature. The cooling tower basin and pump forebay provide 15 minutes of storage of the total circulating rate of 59,536 GPM water. Cooling water is required for the following consumers. Two numbers separate pumping groups are considered for supplying water to the various consumers. • CCS heat exchangers and other misc. consumer- 55,230 GPM Attachment-7: Initial Engineering Design and Cost Estimate 19 DE-FE0031937 / 0009 • Compressor cooling- 568 GPM • Boiler, GT, and others – 3,738 GPM Cooling water makeup is estimated based on four and a half cycles of concentration. A small blowdown stream from the basin is discharged to the plant boundary limit to control the total dissolved solids build- up in the CW circuit. Chemicals such as scale inhibitors and corrosion inhibitors are injected into the make- up and the circulating streams to inhibit corrosion and fouling in the CW system.
